edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Continuous glucose monitoring changes behavior and medication timing by making hyperglycemia visible in real time, which is the route to lower HbA1c.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Zhu meta analysis in BMC Endocr Disord already points to continuous glucose monitoring in type 2 diabetes tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
